newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buyers pull back from German grain market.
newsitem.headline: Buyers pull back from German grain market.

text.p: Rains in European grain areas and EU plans to tax wheat exports are weighing on German prices and prompting an exodus of buyers, brokers said on Wednesday.
"Sellers are trying to get rid of old crop material but cannot place it," one said.
"Buyers feel confident the prices will fall further over the next few weeks."
The EU Commission is expected to approve a tax on daily wheat exports later on Wednesday.
The Hamburg grain exchange cut its wheat (12.5 percent, 220 Hagberg) price free Hamburg by 2.50 marks to 285 marks a tonne but left spot feed wheat unchanged at 280.
Traders said they expected a steady easing rather than a free fall in German prices because of underlying milling industry demand at home and abroad.
Fob Baltic sellers dropped nominal May delivery wheat by between 1.50 and 5.00 marks on the week.
They quoted 12 percent protein wheat at 282.50-198.50 marks and material with 13/14 percent protein at 292.50-318.
Fob Baltic barley and rye offers were little changed at 273.50 and 270-272.50 marks spot respectively.
Old crop supplies were dwindling but buyers held back.
The lethargy spread into the new crop sector, where 12 percent wheat was at parity with May at 282.50 while higher qualities were offered at a steady 292.50-305, basis fob Hamburg.
"The new crop sector would benefit from negative crop weather developments elsewhere in Europe...Germany's crop no longer looks endangered," one broker said.
New crop rye was indicated at around 265-270 and barley at 247.50-255.
